answer: Reputation-weighted task routing. New identities start with zero score and can only accept low-value tasks whose payouts settle after a verification horizon of several weeks. Each identity must hold a small reserve that grows with accepted volume, and this reserve is locked against unresolved disputes. An attacker renting N identities pays N times the reserve plus the full waiting cost before any high-value work, so cost scales linearly while honest throughput stays flat.
